summary: WordPress core gates all AI behind a single function, so it can be killed site-wide with one constant in wp-config.php — before any plugin or theme code runs. This is the only entry on this site where the vendor shipped a real kill switch on purpose.

steps.path: Add the constant to wp-config.php. It runs before plugins, so nothing can override it:
Or filter it programmatically in a small must-use plugin:
UI route: install "Turn Off AI Features" → Settings → General → check "Turn off AI features on this site" (also exposes wp ai disable / enable / status over WP-CLI).

collateral: only affects features that call wp_supports_ai() — a plugin doing its own API calls is unaffected
whyTheyDidIt: Core shipped AI with a documented gate, which is what a healthy default looks like. Individual plugins still have to be audited separately.

sources.label: WordPress.org — Turn Off AI Features plugin (documents WP_AI_SUPPORT and the wp_supports_ai filter)
